strongest_angle: Hungary's government under Prime Minister Péter Magyar fulfilled a major campaign promise on November 4, 2026, by opening communist-era secret police files and launching the searchable online database Nyitottaktak.hu, identifying tens of thousands of former informants after decades of stalled efforts following the 1990 democratic transition.

key_facts.fact: On November 4, 2026, Hungary launched the online database Nyitottaktak.hu to make communist-era secret police files fully accessible, fulfilling a campaign promise by Prime Minister Péter Magyar.
Hungary released communist-era secret police files on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, identifying tens of thousands of former informants in archives spearheaded by Prime Minister Péter Magyar.
Efforts to open communist-era archives in Hungary had repeatedly stalled since the country's democratic transition in 1990 until their release in November 2026.
Thousands of communist-era secret police records were released to the public in Hungary on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, in a searchable online database.
